The Stevens-Johnson-syndrome and toxic-epidermal-necrolysis catalog identities are distinguished from EM in modern consensus classification (lesion morphology, distribution, mucosal severity), so no SJS/TEN-progression edge exists to author - the historical EM-major overlap is classification context, not a disease pathway (negative screen).

Corneal scarring and ocular-surface outcomes belong to the SJS/TEN and severe-scleral-disease identities (Tuft 1991 documents scleral-disease ocular complications), and the scar-target edges would restate resolved-lesion healing. Reopening condition: a cohort quantifying persistent EM-attributable pigmentation beyond the transient resolution window, with a verifiable citation base, would justify re-screening this identity.
